title: Augmented closed-intersection row and canonical comparison data
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $A$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], actual inverse/direct images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and normalized adjunctions [def-sfb-proetale-unit-normalized-adjunction]. Given $i:Z\to X$ and an ordered finite family $W_a\to X$, use the intersection and restriction primitives [def-sfb-closed-intersection-primitives], with the empty index assigned to $Z$. An augmented row is a natural additive functor to integer cochain complexes [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with degree $p$ the finite product of $E_J$ over $|J|-1=p$; its restriction maps obey $\eta_Jr_{J,L}=\eta_L$ for $J\subseteq L$ and are zero otherwise. Its differential is the signed deletion matrix, whose deletion of $a$ has coefficient $(-1)^{\#\{b\in L:b<a\}}r_{L\setminus\{a\},L}$. In a fibre-product square define coefficient transport using the canonical ring compositors. Base-change data consist of the module square comparison normalized by the canonical module compositors and a direct-image comparison whose adjoint is that square comparison followed by the closed counit. Open-compatibility data consist of these base-change data, unit-preserving summand comparisons commuting with all faces, and their augmented-row comparison. At a vertex $a$, contraction data consist of these base-change data, intersection isomorphisms $Z_a\times_XZ_J\cong Z_{J\cup\{a\}}$ over $X$, the unit-preserving augmentation identification $i_a^*E_Z\cong i_a^*$, inverses to $i_a^*r_{J,J\cup\{a\}}$ for $a\notin J$, and natural module maps $h^p:D^p\to D^{p-1}$. Their $J$-component is zero when $a\in J$; otherwise it is $(-1)^{\#\{b\in J:b<a\}}$ times projection to $J\cup\{a\}$ followed by that inverse. They satisfy $dh+hd=1$ in every integer degree. These structures contain the displayed data and identities; defining them asserts no existence.
